sections.h2: Who records deeds in Eaton County, Michigan?
sections.html:
The Eaton County Register of Deeds records deeds, mortgages, lis pendens notices and every other real estate document for the whole county, from Charlotte to Grand Ledge to Eaton Rapids. The office receives each paper, checks it against Michigan recording requirements and stores an image digitally.

Staff do not draft or correct documents. The county's own page says the content and intent of a deed belong to whoever prepared it, and that questions about legal effect go to an attorney. A seller who wants a deed written should ask a title company or a real estate lawyer first, then bring the finished paper to the register.

The counter is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. and closes for lunch from noon to 1:00 p.m. every day. The courthouse also shuts on holidays such as Veterans Day, so check the register's page before a trip. Mailed documents need a self-addressed stamped envelope or the office will not send them back.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Eaton County?
sections.html:
A standard recording in Eaton County costs $30 per document, whether it is a deed, a mortgage, a lis pendens or a certified copy of another real estate paper. The county lists the other charges on its fees page.

Eaton County recording charges listed by the county
ItemCharge
Recording any deed, mortgage or similar document$30
Each extra instrument assigned or discharged in one document$3 added
Tax certificate, up to 25 descriptions$5
Each description past the first 25$0.20
Copy of a real estate record$1 per page
Copy of a recorded plat$2 per page
Certification of a recorded document$1 per page plus $5 for the seal

Certified copies are not offered through the website. Ask at the counter or by mail for those.

sections.h2: What must be in place before Eaton County will record a deed?
sections.html:
The deed needs a tax certificate from the county treasurer when it is a warranty deed, a land contract or an assignment of a land contract. The county cites MCL 211.135 for that rule, and the statute asks for proof that taxes were paid for the five years before the instrument date.

That same statute lists exceptions, including quitclaim deeds and other conveyances without covenants of warranty, sheriff's deeds and tax deeds made by the state treasurer. In practice a title company orders the certificate during closing.

  • A tax certificate from the Eaton County Treasurer for warranty deeds and land contracts.
  • The transfer tax value stated on the face of the deed, or a valuation affidavit attached to it.
  • A self-addressed stamped envelope for mailed filings.
  • The $30 recording fee, plus the $5 certificate fee when one is needed.

A package that falls short is sent back, which can push a closing date. Taxes owed on the parcel, including years in delinquency, have to be settled with the treasurer before the certificate is issued clean.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax applies when an Eaton County house sells?
sections.html:
Two Michigan transfer taxes apply to most sales: the state tax at $3.75 for each $500 of value (MCL 207.525) and the county tax at 55 cents for each $500 in a county under 2,000,000 people (MCL 207.504). Each is charged on the full value, rounded up to the next $500.

The seller owes both under MCL 207.502 and 207.523. The state portion is paid to the county treasurer within 15 days after the deed is delivered.

Take the Census Bureau's 2020-2024 median home value for Eaton County, $216,900, as a worked case. That is 434 units of $500. The state tax is $1,627.50 and the county tax is $238.70, which together come to $1,866.20. A buyer who agrees to cover it in the contract changes who pays at the table, not who the law holds liable.

sections.h2: Which Eaton County transfers are exempt from transfer tax?
sections.html:
Several transfers carry no tax, and the exemption has to be written on the instrument itself. The lists in MCL 207.505 (county) and MCL 207.526 (state) overlap but are not identical.

  • Instruments where the consideration is under $100.
  • Mortgages and other security instruments, and their assignments or discharges.
  • Leases and transfers of leasehold interests.
  • Court judgments or orders that move title without a stated price.
  • Quitclaim deeds that only correct a flaw in title already held.
  • Land contracts, until legal title actually passes.
  • For the state tax, a transfer from a parent to a child or stepchild, and from a grandparent to a grandchild.

If tax was paid on a sale that qualified, MCL 207.523(4) lets the seller or the buyer who paid for the seller ask the state Department of Treasury for a refund.

sections.h2: How do you search Eaton County land records?
sections.html:
The register's online search covers every record from 1836 up to the most recent proof date, so a chain of title can usually be traced from a computer. The link sits on the register's page, next to a link for sending documents electronically.

E-recording matters for sellers because a title company can submit the signed deed without a courier. Ask the closer whether the file will go in electronically and when you should expect the recorded copy. Parcel numbers and tax bills are separate tools, and the county treasurer runs a parcel search for balances due.

sections.h2: What is Eaton County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Eaton County covers 579 square miles of lower Michigan on the western side of Ingham County and Lansing, with 575 square miles of land. It was organized on December 29, 1837 and carries the name of John H. Eaton, President Jackson's secretary of war. Charlotte is the county seat. The other cities are Eaton Rapids, Grand Ledge, Olivet, Potterville and the Eaton County part of Lansing.

Interstates 69, 96 and 496 cross the county, along with state routes such as M-43, M-50 and M-99. Eleven school districts serve the county, among them Charlotte, Eaton Rapids, Grand Ledge, Olivet, Potterville, Maple Valley, Bellevue and Waverly, and a few areas send children to schools in neighboring counties.

The Census Bureau's QuickFacts for 2020-2024 give the local picture:

  • Population estimate of 109,581 for July 2025, with about 48,090 housing units.
  • 74.2% of homes are owner-occupied, against 77.0% in Emmet County.
  • Median household income of $79,597 across 45,428 households.
  • Median gross rent of $1,092 a month.

sections.h2: What happens if property tax on an Eaton County home goes unpaid?
sections.html:
The Eaton County Treasurer collects delinquent taxes and is the foreclosing unit for parcels that stay unpaid. The treasurer's page reports that more than 2,000 foreclosures have been prevented since 2016, and it links a chart of the statutory deadlines for tax foreclosure.

Delinquent bills can be paid online after finding the parcel number and amount through the county's tax search. A 2.49% fee applies to debit and credit card payments, and Lansing city parcels use a separate payment link. The county land bank handles vacant and foreclosed property.

An owner in this position can still sell. The balance is paid from proceeds at closing, and the treasurer's certificate shows the title company what must clear first.

faqs.q: Where is the Eaton County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: The register serves the county from Charlotte, the county seat. The street location is on the register's page at eatoncounty.org, which also lists hours of 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday with a daily lunch closure from noon to 1:00 p.m.

faqs.q: How much is the recording fee in Eaton County?
faqs.a: Thirty dollars per document. Assignments or discharges that cover more than one instrument add $3 for each extra instrument, and a tax certificate costs $5 for up to 25 descriptions.

faqs.q: Can I record a deed online in Eaton County?
faqs.a: Yes, through e-recording. The register's page links an e-record option, and title companies commonly use it. Paper filings by mail must include a self-addressed stamped envelope.

faqs.q: Who pays transfer tax on a house sale in Eaton County?
faqs.a: The seller. Michigan law puts both the state and county transfer tax on the grantor, though a contract can assign the cost to the buyer. The state portion is due to the county treasurer within 15 days after delivery of the deed.

faqs.q: How far back do Eaton County land records go?
faqs.a: The online search runs from 1836 to the latest proof date. For older or certified copies, contact the register's office directly.
